subject: visual-arts
question: 評賞作品時，「描述」與「詮釋」是兩個不同的步驟。試說明兩者的分別，並各舉一句例子。
questionEn: Describing and interpreting are distinct steps in responding to a work. Explain the difference, and give one sentence illustrating each.
explanation: 本題考核評賞方法的基本區分。例句是關鍵：描述句須是任何觀者都同意的事實陳述，詮釋句須包含判斷。
explanationEn: This tests a basic distinction in critical method. The example sentences are decisive: a description must be a statement any viewer would accept, and an interpretation must contain a judgement.
referenceAnswer:
分別：
描述是記錄畫面上客觀可見之事 —— 有甚麼物象、顏色、形狀、位置、大小、質感、構圖安排。描述句的檢驗標準是：任何視力正常的觀者站在作品前，都會同意這句話。
詮釋是就這些可見之事說明其意義、情緒或作用 —— 它提出一個觀者【看不到但可以推論】的主張，因而可以被質疑，亦需要證據支持。
例句：
描述——「畫面左下方有一張空椅，椅背向外，佔畫面約六分之一；室內其餘部分為深褐色，唯獨椅面受光。」
詮釋——「那張受光的空椅暗示一個剛離開或尚未歸來的人，畫家以缺席而非在場來表達思念。」
兩者的關係：
詮釋必須由描述支撐。上例的詮釋之所以站得住，是因為它建基於三項已描述的事實：椅是空的、它受光、其餘部分在暗處。若把這些事實抽走，該詮釋便成為憑空之言。
常見錯誤是跳過描述直接詮釋（「呢幅畫好孤獨」），結果是無法說明何以得出此結論，論述亦無從討論 —— 因為冇共同的觀察基礎。
次序上應先描述後詮釋；但實際寫作時，兩者可以交織，只要每一項詮釋都能指回具體的畫面證據。
referenceAnswerEn:
Difference: description records what is objectively visible in the work — what objects appear, their colours, shapes, positions, sizes, textures and compositional arrangement. The test of a descriptive sentence is that any viewer of normal sight standing before the work would agree with it.
Interpretation states what those visible things mean, feel like or do. It advances a claim the viewer cannot see but can infer, and is therefore open to challenge and in need of evidence.
Examples. Description: 'An empty chair stands at the lower left, its back turned outwards, occupying about a sixth of the picture; the rest of the interior is dark brown, and only the seat catches the light.'
Interpretation: 'The lit empty chair implies someone who has just left or has not yet returned; the painter conveys longing through absence rather than presence.'
The relation between them: interpretation must rest on description. The interpretation above holds because it is built on three described facts — the chair is empty, it is lit, the rest is in shadow. Remove those facts and the interpretation floats free.
The common error is to skip description and interpret at once ('this painting is lonely'), which leaves the writer unable to show how the conclusion was reached and the reader with nothing to discuss, since there is no shared basis of observation.
Description should come first in order, though in writing the two may interweave, provided every interpretation can point back to specific visual evidence.

subject: visual-arts
question: 色彩的「明度」與「彩度」常被混淆。試說明兩者的分別，並指出加入白色顏料時兩者各自如何變化。
questionEn: Value and saturation are often confused. Explain the difference, and state how each changes when white pigment is added.
explanation: 本題須清楚界定兩個獨立維度，並指出加白時兩者【同時】變化 —— 後者正是混淆的來源。
explanationEn: The answer must define two independent dimensions and note that adding white changes both at once, which is the source of the confusion.
referenceAnswer:
分別：
明度指顏色的明暗程度，即該色接近白抑或接近黑。純黃的明度高，純紫的明度低 —— 即使兩者同為飽和的純色。
彩度（又稱純度、飽和度）指顏色的鮮豔程度，即該色含有多少灰。同一個紅色可以由鮮紅漸變至灰紅，明度可以保持不變，變的只是彩度。
兩者是獨立的維度：可以有高明度低彩度的顏色（淺灰粉），亦可以有低明度高彩度的顏色（深而鮮的寶藍）。
加入白色顏料時的變化：
明度——【上升】。混入白色使反射光量增加，顏色變淺。
彩度——【下降】。白色本身無色相，加入之後原色相在混合物中的比例被稀釋，顏色變得柔和、粉質，鮮豔度降低。
即是說，加白會【同時】改變兩個維度，而且方向相反。此正是兩者易被混淆的原因：日常說「調淺啲」時，實際同時發生了明度上升與彩度下降，觀察者難以把兩者分開。
若只想提高明度而盡量保持彩度，畫家的做法是改用本身明度較高的同色相顏料（例如以檸檬黃取代中黃），或在水彩中以加水稀釋並倚靠紙白，而非直接加白顏料。
（加黑則明度下降、彩度亦下降；加該色的補色可在明度變化較小的情況下降低彩度 —— 此為降彩度而不「粉化」的常用方法。）
referenceAnswerEn:
Difference: value is how light or dark a colour is — how near it stands to white or to black. Pure yellow is high in value and pure violet low, even though both are fully saturated.
Saturation, also called chroma or purity, is how vivid a colour is — how much grey it contains. A single red may run from vivid to greyish while its value stays the same; only saturation has changed.
The two are independent dimensions: a colour may be high in value and low in saturation, like a pale dusty pink, or low in value and high in saturation, like a deep vivid ultramarine.
Adding white: value rises, because more light is reflected and the colour becomes lighter. Saturation falls, because white has no hue of its own, so the proportion of the original hue in the mixture is diluted and the colour becomes soft and chalky.
Adding white therefore changes both dimensions at once, and in opposite directions. This is exactly why the two are confused: when people speak of lightening a colour, value is rising and saturation falling together, and the eye finds them hard to separate.
A painter who wants higher value while keeping saturation uses a pigment of the same hue that is naturally lighter — lemon yellow instead of a mid yellow — or, in watercolour, dilutes with water and relies on the white of the paper rather than adding white pigment.
(Adding black lowers both value and saturation; adding a colour's complement lowers saturation with comparatively little change in value, which is the usual way to dull a colour without making it chalky.)

subject: visual-arts
question: 水彩與油畫在「修改」方面的可能性差異極大。試說明此一差異的技術原因，並指出它如何影響兩者的作畫程序。
questionEn: Watercolour and oil differ greatly in how far a work can be revised. Explain the technical reason, and say how this shapes the working procedure of each.
explanation: 本題須由媒材的物理性質推出程序差異，而非只說「水彩唔改得」。第二問要求指出兩種相反的作畫次序。
explanationEn: The answer must derive procedure from the physical properties of the media rather than state that watercolour cannot be corrected, and must identify two opposite working orders.
referenceAnswer:
技術原因：
水彩以水為媒介，顏料顆粒極細，附著於紙張纖維之間並滲入紙面。乾透後顏料已與紙結合，難以完全洗除；且水彩為【透明】顏料，後加的顏色會與底層疊加而非覆蓋 —— 想以淺色蓋深色在物理上不可能，因為淺色透明，底下的深色照樣透出。紙白是唯一的白，一旦被顏料覆蓋便不能取回。
油畫以油為媒介，顏料具遮蓋力（尤其加入鈦白等不透明顏料後），且乾燥緩慢。濕潤時可直接刮除或抹走；乾透後亦可在上面完全覆蓋重畫，下層不會透出。故修改的次數幾乎不受限制。
對作畫程序的影響：
水彩——【由淺至深】，並須預留白位。
畫家須在落筆之前規劃哪些位置保留紙白（高光、雲、水面反光），必要時以留白膠遮蓋。上色次序為先淺後深、先大面後細節，因為深色一旦落下便無法退回。此一限制使水彩高度倚賴【事前計劃】，作畫過程接近執行一個已想清楚的方案。
油畫——【由深至淺】，可邊畫邊改。
傳統做法先鋪暗部與中間調，最後才點上高光，因為不透明的淺色可以蓋在深色之上。畫家可在作畫過程中不斷調整構圖、移動物象、改變光源。此一自由使油畫可以【邊畫邊想】，方案在過程中成形。
（另有「肥蓋瘦」原則：含油量較高的顏料須畫在含油量較低的層之上，否則上層先乾而下層仍在收縮，會導致龜裂 —— 此為油畫可層層覆蓋所帶來的額外規則。）
總結：媒材的可逆性決定了計劃與執行之間的比重。水彩把思考前置，油畫容許思考與執行並行。
referenceAnswerEn:
Technical reason: watercolour uses water as its medium, and its very fine particles lodge among the paper fibres and sink into the surface. Once dry the pigment is bound to the paper and cannot be fully washed out; and watercolour is transparent, so later colour combines with what lies beneath rather than covering it. Putting a light colour over a dark one is physically impossible, since the light colour is transparent and the dark shows through. The white of the paper is the only white, and once covered it cannot be recovered.
Oil uses oil as its medium, its pigments have covering power, especially with opaque whites such as titanium, and it dries slowly. While wet it can be scraped or wiped away; once dry it can be painted over completely without the lower layer showing. Revision is therefore almost unlimited.
Effect on procedure: watercolour works from light to dark and must reserve its whites. The painter decides before starting which areas will keep the paper white — highlights, clouds, reflections on water — masking them if necessary. Colour is laid light before dark and broad before detailed, because once a dark is down it cannot be taken back. This makes watercolour heavily dependent on planning, and the act of painting comes close to executing a scheme already worked out.
Oil works from dark to light and can be revised as it goes. The traditional procedure lays in shadows and mid-tones first and adds highlights last, since opaque light colours cover darks. The painter can keep adjusting composition, moving objects and changing the light source. This freedom lets thinking and painting proceed together, the scheme taking shape in the making.
(A further rule, fat over lean, requires more oily paint to go over less oily layers; otherwise the upper layer dries first while the lower is still contracting, and cracking follows — an additional constraint arising from oil's very capacity to be layered.)
In sum, the reversibility of the medium sets the balance between planning and execution. Watercolour puts the thinking first; oil allows thinking and execution to run together.

subject: visual-arts
question: 文藝復興時期的線性透視法改變了繪畫空間的呈現方式。試說明其基本原理，並指出此一方法所預設的觀看條件。
questionEn: Linear perspective changed how pictorial space was represented in the Renaissance. Explain its basic principle, and state the conditions of viewing it presupposes.
explanation: 第二問是重點，考核考生知否透視法是一套約定而非「正確的看法」。答卷須指出其預設的單眼、固定位置等條件。
explanationEn: The second part is the focus and tests whether the candidate knows that perspective is a convention rather than the correct way of seeing. The presuppositions of a single fixed eye must be identified.
referenceAnswer:
基本原理：
線性透視法假設畫面是一扇「窗」，觀者透過它看向一個三維空間。所有在現實中互相平行、且與畫面垂直的線，在畫中會匯聚於地平線上的同一點，即消失點。
物體的大小按其與觀者的距離成比例縮小：距離加倍，視覺高度減半。地面上等距的物件在畫中的間距亦依此規律遞減。
以一點透視為例：正對觀者的立方體，其側面的邊線全部指向單一消失點；加入第二個消失點則成兩點透視，適用於斜角觀看的物體。
此方法使畫面空間具備可計算的一致性 —— 畫中任一物件的大小與位置，皆可由幾何推算而非憑感覺安排。
所預設的觀看條件：
一、單一眼睛。透視投影由一個點出發。但人有雙眼，兩眼所見略有差異，真實視覺包含雙眼視差。透視畫面對應的是閉上一隻眼所見。
二、固定位置且不轉動。觀者須站在特定的一點（正對消失點、距離與畫幅有既定比例），頭與眼均不移動。實際觀畫時人會走動、轉頭，故大多數時候所見與理論位置並不吻合。
三、平面的投影面。人的視網膜是曲面，而透視法投影到平面上。故廣角構圖的邊緣會出現在幾何上正確、但看來扭曲的形變（例如邊緣的圓柱變成橢圓）。
四、靜止的一瞬。它呈現的是單一時刻的單一視點，排除了時間與移動。
由此可見，線性透視並非「事物本來的樣子」，而是一套為特定觀看條件而設的約定。認識到這一點，便能理解為何其他傳統（如中國山水的散點構圖、埃及壁畫的正面律）並非「未掌握透視」，而是依據不同的呈現目的採用不同的約定 —— 前者容許觀者在畫中遊走，後者則要求每一部分以其最可辨認的角度呈現。
referenceAnswerEn:
Basic principle: linear perspective treats the picture plane as a window through which the viewer looks into a three-dimensional space. Lines that are parallel in reality and perpendicular to the picture plane converge in the picture on a single point on the horizon, the vanishing point.
Objects diminish in proportion to their distance from the viewer: double the distance, half the apparent height. Equally spaced objects on the ground diminish in their intervals by the same rule.
In one-point perspective, a cube facing the viewer has all its receding edges directed to a single vanishing point; adding a second point gives two-point perspective, suited to objects seen at an angle.
The method gives pictorial space a calculable consistency: the size and position of any object can be derived geometrically rather than judged by feel.
Conditions of viewing presupposed: first, a single eye, since the projection issues from one point. Human beings have two eyes whose views differ slightly, and real vision includes binocular disparity; a perspective picture corresponds to what is seen with one eye closed.
Second, a fixed position without turning. The viewer must stand at a particular point, facing the vanishing point at a set distance relative to the picture, with head and eye still. In practice people move and turn, so what is seen rarely matches the theoretical position.
Third, a flat projection surface. The retina is curved while perspective projects onto a plane, so the edges of a wide composition show distortions that are geometrically correct yet look wrong — a cylinder at the edge becoming an ellipse.
Fourth, a single instant: one viewpoint at one moment, excluding time and movement.
Linear perspective is therefore not how things are but a convention devised for particular conditions of viewing. Recognising this explains why other traditions — the shifting viewpoints of Chinese landscape, the frontality of Egyptian wall painting — are not failures to grasp perspective but different conventions serving different purposes: the first lets the viewer travel through the picture, the second requires each part to be shown from its most recognisable angle.

subject: visual-arts
question: 中國書畫中的「留白」並非未完成的部分。試說明留白在畫面上的兩項作用，並解釋它與西方繪畫處理背景的方式有何不同。
questionEn: Blank space in Chinese painting and calligraphy is not an unfinished area. Describe two of its functions, and explain how it differs from the treatment of background in Western painting.
explanation: 本題須把留白視為積極的構成元素。比較部分要指出兩種傳統對「空」的根本態度差異。
explanationEn: The answer must treat blank space as an active compositional element, and the comparison must identify a fundamental difference in attitude towards emptiness.
referenceAnswer:
留白的兩項作用：
一、構成空間與氣韻。留白並非「甚麼都沒有」，而是承擔具體的空間意義：山腰的空白讀作雲霧，山腳的空白讀作水面，人物之間的空白讀作距離。觀者依據周圍物象的提示，把空白填入相應的內容。此一機制使畫面得以在有限的筆墨之內呈現廣闊的空間。
同時，空白處讓密處得以喘息，形成疏密節奏 —— 所謂「疏可走馬，密不透風」，兩者互為條件：無疏則密不成其為密。
二、留予觀者參與。空白不作明確界定，觀者須以自身經驗補足。此一補足的過程使觀看由被動接收轉為主動參與，而各人所補足的未必相同，作品因而具有詮釋的彈性。
（第三項作用：承載題款、印章與詩文，使書、畫、印在同一畫面中構成整體。）
與西方繪畫處理背景的不同：
西方傳統（尤其文藝復興至十九世紀）傾向【填滿】畫面。背景是需要描繪的對象：天空有雲與漸變的色階，室內有牆壁、家具與光影，即使暗處亦以顏料鋪滿。空白畫布被視為未完成的狀態。
這一取態與其目標一致：既然畫面模擬一扇望向真實空間的窗，而真實空間中並不存在「甚麼都沒有的區域」，畫面自然不應留下空白。
中國書畫的空白則是【經營】出來的。它由筆墨的位置界定，其形狀、大小與位置皆屬構圖決定，與落筆之處同樣重要。故有「計白當黑」之說 —— 空白被當作與墨色同等的構成元素來安排。
根本差異在於：西方傳統中的空是【尚未被填滿的地方】，中國傳統中的空是【被安排出來的存在】。前者是缺席，後者是在場。
referenceAnswerEn:
Two functions of blank space: first, it constitutes space and atmosphere. Blank is not nothing; it carries specific spatial meaning — blank at the waist of a mountain reads as cloud, blank at its foot as water, blank between figures as distance. Guided by the surrounding forms, the viewer fills the void with the appropriate content, which lets a painting present vast space with limited brushwork.
Blank also lets dense passages breathe, creating a rhythm of sparse and dense. The two are mutually conditioning: without sparseness, density would not register as density.
Second, it leaves room for the viewer to take part. Because the blank is not defined, the viewer must complete it from their own experience, so looking becomes active rather than receptive, and since different viewers complete it differently the work retains interpretative flexibility.
(A third function: it carries inscription, seal and poem, so that calligraphy, painting and seal form a single whole.)
Difference from the Western treatment of background: the Western tradition, especially from the Renaissance to the nineteenth century, tends to fill the picture. The background is something to be depicted: sky with clouds and graded tone, interiors with walls, furniture and cast light, and even shadow laid in with paint. Bare canvas counts as unfinished.
That attitude follows from the aim: if the picture imitates a window onto real space, and real space contains no region where there is nothing, then no blank should remain.
Blank in Chinese painting is by contrast composed. It is defined by where the brush is placed, and its shape, size and position are compositional decisions as consequential as the marks themselves — hence the saying that the white is reckoned as the black, the void arranged as an element equal to ink.
The fundamental difference: in the Western tradition emptiness is a place not yet filled; in the Chinese tradition it is something arranged into being. The first is absence, the second presence.

subject: visual-arts
question: 同一件作品在不同展示脈絡中（美術館、宗教場所、商場），觀者的理解可能不同。試分析展示脈絡如何影響意義的形成。
questionEn: The same work may be understood differently in a museum, a place of worship or a shopping mall. Analyse how the context of display shapes meaning.
explanation: 本題須指出脈絡不只是背景，而是參與意義形成的條件。答卷宜就不同場所各舉具體機制。
explanationEn: The answer must show that context is not mere background but a condition participating in the making of meaning, with a specific mechanism for each setting.
referenceAnswer:
脈絡影響意義的機制：
一、觀看的姿態由場所預先設定。
進入美術館的人已預期自己要「欣賞」：放慢腳步、保持距離、閱讀標籤、尋找作品的藝術價值。同一件宗教雕像在美術館中，其技法、年代與風格成為關注焦點。
而在宗教場所，同一雕像的觀看姿態是敬拜：信眾不是在「看一件作品」，而是在面對一個具體的對象。此時技法是否精湛並非重點，甚至不被注意。
在商場，觀看姿態是掃視。人流不為此而來，作品被歸入環境裝飾一類，多數人不會停下。
二、脈絡賦予「這值得注意」的信號。
美術館的白牆、射燈、基座與標籤共同宣告：此物已被篩選，值得認真對待。此一制度性認可本身就構成意義的一部分 —— 同一件物品置於路邊，多數人不會視之為藝術。
三、脈絡決定可用的解讀框架。
宗教場所提供教義框架，觀者以象徵與典故理解作品；美術館提供藝術史框架，觀者以流派與影響理解作品；商場提供消費框架，觀者可能理解為品牌形象或打卡背景。同一組視覺元素，在不同框架下指向不同內容。
四、脈絡影響身體與時間。
美術館要求安靜與步行，觀看時間由觀者自主；宗教儀式中觀看時間由儀式節奏決定；商場的觀看是移動中的、被打斷的。停留時間直接影響可被察覺的細節層次。
五、脈絡本身可能改變作品的物理狀態與完整性。
宗教造像原本置於特定光線、香火與空間關係之中，被移入美術館後脫離原境，其原有的部分意義隨之流失 —— 這是文物「去脈絡化」的常見問題。
綜合：
作品的意義並非完全內在於物件本身，而是在物件與觀者、場所、既有知識的互動中形成。故同一件作品的意義會隨脈絡改變，並不代表某一種理解是錯的；但須注意，脈絡的轉移可能令原有脈絡中的意義變得不可見，而觀者往往不會察覺自己失去了甚麼。
referenceAnswerEn:
How context shapes meaning. First, the setting presets the posture of viewing. Someone entering a museum already expects to appreciate: they slow down, keep a distance, read labels and look for artistic value. A religious sculpture in a museum is attended to for its technique, date and style.
In a place of worship the posture is devotional: the worshipper is not looking at a work but facing a particular presence, and whether the carving is skilful is beside the point and may not be noticed at all.
In a shopping mall the posture is scanning. People are not there for this, the work is filed under décor, and most do not stop.
Second, context signals that something is worth attention. White walls, spotlights, plinths and labels together announce that this object has been selected and deserves serious attention. That institutional endorsement is itself part of the meaning: the same object at the roadside would not be taken for art by most people.
Third, context supplies the interpretive frame available. A place of worship supplies a doctrinal frame, and the viewer reads through symbol and story; a museum supplies an art-historical frame, and the viewer reads through movement and influence; a mall supplies a commercial frame, and the work may be read as brand image or a backdrop for photographs. The same visual elements point to different content under different frames.
Fourth, context governs body and time. A museum asks for quiet and walking, and the viewer sets the duration; in a rite the duration is set by the liturgy; in a mall viewing is mobile and interrupted. How long one stays directly affects what level of detail can be noticed.
Fifth, context may alter the physical state and integrity of the work. A devotional image was made for particular light, incense and spatial relations, and moving it into a museum severs those, so part of its original meaning is lost — the familiar problem of decontextualised objects.
In sum, meaning is not wholly inside the object but arises in the interaction of object, viewer, setting and prior knowledge. That meaning shifts with context does not make any one reading wrong; but it is worth noting that a shift of context can make the meaning of the original setting invisible, and viewers seldom notice what they have lost.

subject: visual-arts
question: 有觀眾認為當代藝術「技法門檻低，人人都做得到」。試分析此一評價背後的判斷標準，並說明為何以技法作為唯一標準會出現困難。
questionEn: Some viewers hold that contemporary art requires little skill and anyone could do it. Analyse the criterion behind that judgement, and explain the difficulty of using technical skill as the sole standard.
explanation: 本題須先還原對方的立場再加以檢視，不可直接斥為無知。答卷宜指出技法標準在甚麼情況下仍然成立。
explanationEn: The position must first be reconstructed and then examined, not dismissed as ignorance, and the answer should note where the technical criterion still holds.
referenceAnswer:
評價背後的判斷標準：
此一評價預設「藝術價值 ＝ 製作難度」。其邏輯是：作品之所以值得欣賞，因為它體現了常人做不到的技藝；難度愈高、耗時愈久、愈需長期訓練，價值愈高。
這一標準並非無理。它在歷史上長期有效：從文藝復興到十九世紀，寫實再現的能力確實是稀缺的，畫家的訓練以年計，而其成果無法由未受訓者複製。在該脈絡下，技法既是門檻，亦是價值的可靠指標。
此一標準亦有實際優點：它可被觀察、可被比較，不依賴專門知識。任何人站在一幅精細的油畫前，都能判斷它不易做到。
以技法為唯一標準的困難：
一、技法的稀缺性已經改變。攝影出現之後，寫實再現不再是繪畫獨有的能力；而數位工具進一步降低了多項技術的門檻。若價值僅繫於稀缺的手藝，則價值會隨技術普及而自動消失 —— 這個結論多數人並不接受。
二、「人人都做得到」與「人人都做咗」是兩回事。此類評語通常在作品完成之後才出現。難度的一部分不在執行，而在【想到】以及【決定這樣做】—— 即在無數可能之中選擇這一個，並承擔它可能不被接受的風險。事後複製一個已被指出的做法，與事前提出它，並不等價。
三、標準無法涵蓋部分作品的實際內容。觀念藝術、行為藝術、裝置與場域特定作品，其核心在於提出的問題、與空間的關係、或觀者的參與。以技法衡量它們，如同以字數衡量一首詩 —— 量度的是一個與作品目標無關的維度。
四、技法本身亦非單一。當代作品的技術難度可能不在手繪，而在材料工程、程式編寫、物流與協作規模。觀眾未見到這些工序，便誤以為不存在。
仍然成立之處：
技法標準並非全然失效。若一件作品本身訴諸手藝（寫實繪畫、工藝、書法），則以技法評價完全恰當。困難只在於把單一標準套用於所有作品。
較可行的取態：
先問「這件作品試圖做甚麼」，再問「它是否做到」。評賞標準應隨作品的目標而定，而非預先固定。這不等於一切皆可 —— 作品若連自身設定的目標亦未達成，批評依然成立，而且比「無技法」更為有力。
referenceAnswerEn:
The criterion behind the judgement: it assumes that artistic value equals difficulty of making. The reasoning is that a work merits attention because it embodies a skill ordinary people lack, and that the harder, the more time-consuming and the more dependent on long training, the greater the value.
The standard is not unreasonable. It held for a long time historically: from the Renaissance to the nineteenth century the ability to represent convincingly was genuinely scarce, a painter's training took years, and the result could not be reproduced by the untrained. In that context technique was both a threshold and a reliable index of value.
It also has a practical merit: it can be observed and compared without specialist knowledge. Anyone standing before a finely worked painting can tell it was not easy.
Difficulties with it as the sole standard: first, the scarcity of technique has changed. After photography, convincing representation was no longer painting's alone, and digital tools have lowered other thresholds further. If value rests only on scarce handcraft, value disappears automatically as the craft becomes common — a conclusion most people do not accept.
Second, 'anyone could do it' and 'anyone did do it' are different claims. Such remarks are made after the fact. Part of the difficulty lies not in execution but in conceiving the idea and deciding to act on it — selecting this possibility among countless others and bearing the risk that it will not be accepted. Reproducing an approach once it has been pointed out is not equivalent to proposing it beforehand.
Third, the standard does not reach the actual content of some works. In conceptual art, performance, installation and site-specific work, what matters is the question raised, the relation to the space or the viewer's participation. Judging these by technique is like judging a poem by word count: it measures a dimension unrelated to the work's aim.
Fourth, technique itself is not one thing. The technical difficulty of contemporary work may lie in materials engineering, programming, logistics or the scale of collaboration rather than in hand drawing, and viewers who do not see those processes assume they are absent.
Where the criterion still holds: it has not become useless. Where a work itself appeals to craft — representational painting, applied art, calligraphy — judging it by technique is entirely apt. The difficulty is only in applying a single standard to every work.
A more workable stance: ask first what the work is trying to do, and then whether it does it. Criteria should follow the aim of the work rather than be fixed in advance. This is not to say anything goes: where a work fails even the aim it sets itself, criticism holds — and is more telling than an accusation of lacking technique.

subject: visual-arts
question: 評賞作品時，「作者原意」應佔多大比重？試就此問題提出你的看法，並處理一項與你立場相反的論點。
questionEn: How much weight should an artist's intention carry in criticism? State your position, and address one argument against it.
explanation: 本題要求表明立場並主動處理反方論點，兩者缺一不可。只列舉雙方觀點而不作判斷，未完成作答。
explanationEn: A position must be stated and a counter-argument addressed; both are required. Setting out both sides without reaching a judgement leaves the task incomplete.
referenceAnswer:
立場：
作者原意是【重要的證據之一】，但不是決定性的標準。
理由：
一、原意往往不可得。多數歷史作品的作者未留下說明；即使有書信或訪談，那亦只是作者在某一時刻的自述，未必等同創作當時的實際意圖，亦可能經過事後整理。以一個難以確定的東西作為判準，會令評賞失去可操作性。
二、作品完成後即獨立於作者。觀者所面對的是物件本身。若作品的實際效果與作者所述不符 —— 例如作者聲稱要表達希望，而畫面的色調與構圖讀來壓抑 —— 我們應以可見的證據為準，因為那才是所有觀者共同面對的。
三、作品可能超出作者的自覺。畫家所處時代的視覺習慣、社會關係與潛在偏見，會進入作品而作者未必自知。這些內容是作品的一部分，卻不在原意之內；若只以原意為限，這一層完全無法討論。
四、但原意仍是重要證據。它能提供脈絡、排除明顯錯誤的解讀、指出作者所面對的問題。無視原意的詮釋容易變成投射 —— 觀者只在作品中看見自己想看的東西。
故較恰當的位置是：原意作為【約束詮釋的參考】而非【裁決詮釋的權威】。詮釋須能被畫面證據支撐，而原意是眾多證據中份量較重的一項。
處理一項相反論點：
反方會說：「若不以作者原意為準，詮釋便無底線，任何說法都可以成立。」
這一憂慮是合理的，但推論並不成立。放棄原意作為唯一權威，並不等於放棄一切標準。詮釋仍受三項約束：
一、畫面證據。詮釋必須指得出具體的形式依據；指不出的即為臆測。
二、脈絡證據。作品的年代、媒材、創作背景與同期作品構成可查證的框架，明顯違反此框架的解讀可被排除。
三、融貫性。一個能解釋作品較多特徵的詮釋，優於只能解釋個別細節而與其餘部分矛盾的詮釋。
有了這三項，詮釋之間仍可比較高下 —— 有些詮釋確實比另一些更有說服力。故「非此即彼」（不是原意權威，就是全無標準）本身是一個假二分：標準的來源不只一個。
referenceAnswerEn:
Position: the artist's intention is one important piece of evidence, but not a decisive standard.
Reasons: first, intention is often unavailable. Most historical works come with no statement from their makers, and where letters or interviews exist they record what the artist said at one moment, which need not match the intention at the time of making and may have been tidied afterwards. Making an uncertain thing the criterion leaves criticism unworkable.
Second, a finished work stands apart from its maker. What the viewer confronts is the object. Where the effect of the work differs from what the artist reports — the artist says the subject is hope while the tonality and composition read as oppressive — the visible evidence should govern, since that is what all viewers share.
Third, a work may exceed the artist's awareness. The visual habits, social relations and latent assumptions of a period enter the work without the maker necessarily knowing. That content belongs to the work but lies outside the intention, and confining criticism to intention makes it undiscussable.
Fourth, intention nonetheless remains important evidence. It supplies context, rules out plainly mistaken readings and identifies the problem the artist was addressing. Interpretation that ignores it easily becomes projection, the viewer finding in the work only what they came to see.
The appropriate position is therefore that intention constrains interpretation as a reference rather than adjudicating it as an authority: readings must be supported by visual evidence, and intention is one of the weightier pieces among that evidence.
Addressing a counter-argument: it may be objected that without intention as the standard, interpretation has no limit and any claim will do.
The concern is reasonable but the inference does not follow. Abandoning intention as the sole authority is not abandoning all standards. Interpretation remains bound by three things. Visual evidence: a reading must point to specific formal grounds, and one that cannot is speculation. Contextual evidence: date, medium, circumstances of making and contemporaneous works form a checkable frame, and readings that plainly violate it can be excluded. Coherence: an interpretation that accounts for more features of the work is better than one that explains an isolated detail while contradicting the rest.
With these, interpretations can still be ranked — some really are more persuasive than others. The either-or, that we must choose between the authority of intention and no standards at all, is a false dichotomy: standards come from more than one source.
